title: Attention fixed cost: sliding-verify window path and FA3 full verify at small B

designs.title: swf: one cluster launch per sliding-verify step (in-kernel pre-attention, the board's wgmma window tile body, DSMEM reduce-scatter merge with norm-gate), attention B=1..32 first, then a decode port with PDL
designs.angle: Fuse and trim the window path. Each sliding-verify step becomes one launch with no global workspace, ticket or fence. That launch covers what today takes pre-attention, then the window kernel, then the PDL combine (B=2..32), or pre-attention, then the PSEUDO stream-K kernel (B=1). The combine goes into the kernel as a fixed-size thread-block-cluster merge over distributed shared memory (DSMEM). This differs in mechanism from the refuted global ticket merge ("tk"). The prologue and launch cuts: one seqlen load instead of the all-B tile-prefix scan; page indices loaded straight from the request's row; the whole per-CTA tile set put in flight at once; q and new-K/V work moved into the shadow of the seqlen -> page-table -> KV chain. PDL is only needed where a kernel boundary remains, which is decode's QKV GEMM -> swf and swf -> o GEMM.

designs.floor:
TASK.md floors, from reference.speed_of_light_ns at 4.8 TB/s and 989 TFLOP/s:
- verify 1: tokens = 1 x 2048 x 1.0. Bytes = 2048 x 2 x 64 x 2 = 524,288, plus the qkv/out term 1 x 8 x 36 x 64 x 2 x 2 = 73,728, total 598,016 B -> 0.125 us. FLOPs = 4 x 2048 x 8 x 16 x 64 = 67 M -> 0.07 us. Floor 0.12 us.
- verify 16: tokens = 16 x 2048 x 0.925 = 30,310. Bytes = 7.76 MB + 1.18 MB = 8.94 MB -> 1.86 us. FLOPs 0.99 G -> 1.0 us. Floor 1.86 us.
- verify 32: 17.9 MB -> 3.72 us.
So the rows sit at 110x / 10.5x / 7.3x their floor (net): fixed cost, not bytes.

Practical floor for a single-launch structure (what swf cannot avoid):
- a one-node graph costs about 1.0 us of judge net (one_ns 4.90 - overhead 3.90);
- three dependent cold DRAM round trips: seqlen -> page-table entries -> KV rows. The board kernel's K=8 run costs 5.5 us beyond a null kernel, and that includes one tile and the partial stores;
- the KV stream: 0.53 / 8.4 / 16.8 MB (2055 keys x 256 B x B). At today's window-kernel gather rate of 1.1-1.35 TB/s that is +6.4 / +14.8 us beyond K=8. At the 3.0 TB/s the stream-K kernel reaches with the full-line gather it would be 0.2 / 2.8 / 5.6 us;
- a cluster merge of at least ~0.5 us.

Practical floor ≈ 7 / 10 / 13 us net at B=1/16/32 with a 3 TB/s gather, or ≈ 7 / 13 / 21 us at today's gather rate. The leaders' ~8-12 us rows sit at this structure's floor, which is why the remaining fixed cost (launches, pre-attention node, combine node) is the first lever.
designs.mechanism:
KERNEL: swf_kernel<int STAGES=5, bool FULLLINE>, in a new module muse_sliding_verify_fused_v1 (sm_90a only, -O3 -std=c++20).
- Launch: one cudaLaunchKernelEx with cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension = (C,1,1). NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed is set for C=16.
- Shape: grid = B*C, 256 threads, __launch_bounds__(256,2), dynamic smem ≈ 112 KB (fits 2 CTAs per SM).
- Smem layout: ring 5 x 16 KB; V^T 2 heads x 2 buffers x 4 KB; QS 8 KB of per-thread Q fragment words (the board's layout); cos/sin table 2 KB; page-index block up to 576 int32; barriers.
- CTA identity: b = blockIdx.x / C, rank = blockIdx.x % C. Warpgroup g = kv head g, as on the board.

DECOMPOSITION
- seq = cache_seqlens[b] - 8.
- Old keys [max(0, seq - 2047), seq) are tiled from the END: tile t = [seq - 64(t+1), seq - 64t), NT = ceil(min(seq, 2047) / 64). NT = 32 for every scored request.
- Rank r takes old tiles [r*NT/C, (r+1)*NT/C): exactly 2 / 4 / 8 tiles at C = 16 / 8 / 4.
- Rank 0 also owns the 8 new keys as virtual tile v=0, an smem tile in ring stage 0. Its other tiles are v = 1..n.
- Bands and C candidates raced at prepare: B=1 -> C=16 (also race 8); B=2..16 -> C=8 (also 16); B=17..32 -> C=4 (also 8). A C is raced only if cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters at this smem size covers one wave.

DATA MOVEMENT (prologue order)
1. At entry, issue independent loads:
   - cache_seqlens[b];
   - each thread's q words for (token r = lane>>2, heads hA = 8g + 2w and hA+1): 8 x 8 B of bf16 qkv;
   - rank 0 only: the new k and v words (warp = token, lane = RoPE pair; 4 x 4 B) and cache_loc[8b..8b+7].
   Thread 0 initialises the mbarriers with fence.mbarrier_init.
2. Once seq arrives: plain coalesced loads of the page-table entries for this CTA's tiles into the index block, then __syncthreads (which also publishes the mbarrier init).
3. Issue cp.async gathers for every tile that fits the 5-stage ring, all at once, with noinc arrivals on FULL. Use the full-line mapping: thread -> rows tid>>3 and tid>>3+32, chunk tid&7, so each warp instruction covers 4 whole 128-B lines. This is the sk full-line / issue_sub mapping, with the same SW128 destination (c ^ (row & 7)) << 4 as the board.
   - Rows with position < 0 are zero-filled (src-size 0).
   - Row indices are clamped into the cache.
   - The prologue issues STAGES tiles, not STAGES-1. The loop refills only at n >= 1 (C=4: 8-9 tiles).
4. In the gathers' shadow:
   - one sincosf per thread: token tid>>5, pair tid&31, angle (seq + token) * inv_freq; write to the cos/sin table, then __syncthreads;
   - q fragments: RMS via quad shuffles, interleaved RoPE, e4m3 (without the 5.473 factor, exactly as _pre_attention_kernel), sts32 into QS;
   - rank 0: new k = e4m3(RoPE(RMS(k)) / k_scale) and new v = e4m3(v / v_scale), satfinite. Store them to the cache at cache_loc (global; the judge checks these rows) and into stage-0 rows 0..7. Zero rows 8..63 of K and V. Then fence.proxy.async and a plain mbarrier arrive on FULL[0].
   - Then fence.proxy.async and __syncthreads.
5. Main loop: the board's per-tile body, copied verbatim:
   - wait FULL, then fence.proxy.async;
   - S = QK^T as two m64n64k32 e4m3 wgmma steps;
   - the V^T byte transpose into the parity buffer, then EMPTY arrive;
   - mask and online softmax with FA3's Max_offset 8 (exp2 units);
   - P to e4m3, then PV as two wgmma steps.
   Only the mask changes:
   - old tile t: column ct is valid iff ct >= max(64(t+1) - seq, 64(t+1) + r - 2047). The test runs only when 64(t+1) > min(seq, 2040).
   - smem tile: valid iff ct <= r and ct < 8.
   Ranks with no tiles skip the loop with m = -inf, l = 0.

SYNCHRONISATION
- Per-CTA mbarrier ring as on the board. No global atomics, tickets, __threadfence, counters or workspaces.
- After the loop: cp.async.wait_all, wgmma wait, __syncthreads. Then write the partials into the drained ring:
  - O as fp32 [128 rows (token*16 + head)][64], row stride 68 floats;
  - m and l per row (l quad-reduced).
- Then griddepcontrol.launch_dependents (a no-op in attention; in decode it starts the o GEMM's prologue), then barrier.cluster.arrive.release.
- Then issue the gate loads for the rows this rank finalises, then barrier.cluster.wait.acquire.
- Every CTA executes both cluster barriers unconditionally. There is no early return; the mbarrier-timeout path falls through to them.

EPILOGUE: reduce-scatter over DSMEM
- Rank r finalises rows [r*128/C, (r+1)*128/C): 16 threads per row, one float4 each. At C=4 each thread takes 2 rows; at C=16 threads 128-255 idle as whole warps.
- For each row, read (m, l, O float4) of all C ranks through map_shared_rank. Merge in fixed rank order: running max M, rescale by ex2(M_old - M_new); m = -inf weighs 0. This is sw_combine_kernel's arithmetic.
- Multiply by v_scale / L. L > 0 always, because rank 0 holds key p for every token.
- Scaleless RMSNorm over 64 dims (xor shuffles 8, 4, 2, 1), times sigmoid(gate) with accurate expf.
- Store bf16 to out[(8b + j) * 1024 + h * 64 + d].
- A second cluster barrier (arrive after the last DSMEM read, wait before exit) keeps peers' smem alive.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE REFUTED tk
tk (kernel<TICKET>):
- the last-arriving warpgroup, elected by a global atomicAdd after __threadfence, reads every slot's 16 KB fp32 partial back through L2 (9 slots at B=16 grid 128, 17 at grid 264);
- one 128-thread warpgroup, register-capped at 128, then finalises 64 rows;
- it runs inside a CTA whose other warpgroup stalls on the shared ring;
- its cost grows with the slot count: s1 went from 14.9 us at grid 32 to 81.7 us at grid 264, and merge_head costs +15.8-45 us while the ticket-only tail costs only +0.7-2.7 us.
swf:
- partials stay in each CTA's smem and are read over the SM-to-SM cluster network: no global write or read, no fence, no atomic, no reset;
- the merge is spread over all C ranks (16 rows per rank at C=8, each thread reading 8 float4 plus 16 scalars);
- C is fixed (<= 16) and independent of the grid;
- every rank merges exactly once, after its own last tile;
- the form is proven on the board: sliding_cluster_kernel uses cluster.sync + map_shared_rank reduce-scatter inside a 9.6 us kernel (4e386647 profile, decode 1 sliding).
The earlier one-launch attempts lost on compute, not on the merge:
- sliding-cuda-cluster-dsmem-onelaunch used mma.sync for 64 rows per kv head: verify 28.45 / 41.52 / 65.57 us against 17.63 / 22.77 / 29.35;
- sliding-single-launch-fused-attention used Triton with 64-row tiles: 0.945x.
swf keeps the wgmma tile body.
The fold differs from FUSED_PRE (0.988x / 1.014x) and the killed sliding-decode-sk-s3 fold:
- there, q had to be computed per segment inside a stream-K CTA serving several requests;
- here each CTA serves one request, computes q once while 3 dependent cold round trips are in flight, and the fold also removes the new-key straddle, which is what makes the even 32-tile split possible.

GATING
- kernel_fn has a config-only predicate placed right after the sliding-decode branch: `if _SWF_ROUTE and _swf_gate(cfg): return _swf_forward(data)`. The predicate requires window 2048, q_len 8, page 1, 16/2 heads, head dim 64, RoPE on, 1 <= B <= 32 and the band routed.
- _swf_forward allocates out with torch.empty from shapes and makes one cudaLaunchKernelEx.
- _swf_setup() runs after _sw_setup(), so it races against kernel_fn's real routed path: PSEUDO at B=1, sw at B=2..32. It runs:
  1. attrs: regs, local bytes, binaryVersion 90, occupancy per C;
  2. a named canary;
  3. a self-check matrix vs _ps_reference fp32 (rel L2 < 2e-2, finite, error word 0), vs the incumbent's output (< 3e-2) and vs the Triton pre-attention's cache rows on cloned inputs (e4m3 code gap <= 1);
  4. run-to-run bitwise identity;
  5. interleaved cold-L2 graph rounds (2 x 31 reps): fused at each C vs the incumbent, plus fused at lens 0 (the fixed term) and a null kernel. Route iff >= 1.05x (1.03x at B=17..32) in both rounds, with the IQR bound;
  6. a two-state replay (_alt_check, gate=_swf_gate);
  7. freeze _SWF_ROUTE = MappingProxyType({band: C}).
- Print PATH CHOSEN lines, plus a one-line [swf] ROUTES summary after the [paths] re-print.

PDL
- The attention graph is one node, so nothing to place.
- In decode (stage 3) the same binary is PDL-launched after _dsa_gemm('qkv_gate'):
  - before griddepcontrol.wait: steps 1 (without the qkv words), 2, 3 and the cos/sin table, because cache_seqlens, page_table, cache_loc and the old KV rows are step inputs the GEMM does not write;
  - after the wait: the qkv words, q, new K/V and gate;
  - trigger after the main loop for the o GEMM.
- With the PDL attribute absent, griddepcontrol.wait is a no-op, so attention and decode share one source.

Decision rules:
- merge <= 1.2 us at (16,8) and (32,4) and <= 1.0 at (1,16): build as specified.
- QPRO delta <= 0.3 us: fold as specified. If > 0.5 us, the q prologue moves to warps 4-7 only.
- full/half <= 0.97: FULLLINE=1.
- T1 kernel<SPLIT>(B=1, grid 16, K=2048) + 0.9 <= routed PSEUDO step - 2: the B=1 central estimate holds.

designs.rules:
- Graph-capturable. _swf_forward branches only on config and the import-frozen _SWF_ROUTE (MappingProxyType). It does torch.empty(out) from shapes and one cudaLaunchKernelEx with a cluster attribute; the board's sliding_cluster_kernel is captured the same way. No .item(), syncs or data-dependent Python.
- Nothing data-derived cached. No workspace, ticket, counter or flag is read on the timed path. seq, the tile ranges, the page indices, cos/sin and q are all computed in-kernel per call from cache_seqlens, page_table, cache_loc and qkv. The only persistent buffer is the error word, written only on an mbarrier timeout and read only at prepare.
- FP8 KV as given. q is rounded to e4m3 (allowed, as FA3 does). P is e4m3 with FA3's Max_offset 8, as on the board. Accumulation is fp32 (wgmma f32, fp32 merge); the output is bf16; new cache rows are e4m3 with the scales applied.
- Every key attended. The emulator proves the attended set equals reference.py's window per token, exactly once. There is no skipping or sparsity, and no top-k.
- Order-deterministic cross-CTA reduction: DSMEM merge in fixed rank order, no atomics. Copy checks therefore replay bitwise, and the self-check asserts torch.equal across two launches.
- All work inside kernel_fn. Pre-attention, cache store, attention, merge and norm-gate are all in the one launch. Only the build, checks and races run at import.
- Prepare time. Attention has no prepare(); the import clock rule is <= 480 s and the run limit 15 min. Phase starts are guarded by deadlines (build <= 380 s, checks <= 420, final rounds <= 455, replay <= 475); the run grows to about 670 of 900 s. In decode, the swf build joins decode's background-build deadlines inside the 300 s prepare.
- No timing patches, harness frames, reference imports, network or extra processes beyond load_inline's nvcc, as every board does.
- Raced at prepare against kernel_fn's routed path, with canary, self-check, replay and the interleaved A/B. A loss or failure leaves the incumbent; PATH CHOSEN lines name the routed arm.
- Size: attention about 545 KB, under 1,000,000. Decode is within the budget after the listed deletions.
- No GPU before the judge: the emulator, cuda_syntax.py, lint, py_compile and the audit come first. Tonight's T1/T2 are prepare-only and change no route.
- Binding lessons: the merge, fold and gather mapping are schedule claims, so T1/T2 and the in-run gate prints are their judge-side rungs. Gains are claimed only per row and against the 1.2% noise.

designs.risks:
1. Merge cost. DSMEM traffic plus the cluster-barrier skew could exceed 0.9 us, especially at C=16. T2 measures it. At 2.5 us the B=16/32 cuts fall to about -3.5 / -3 us, and swf-pdl becomes the stage-1 form.
2. Fold not hidden. The q prologue (16 regs of qkv, sincosf, RMS/RoPE/e4m3) or rank 0's new K/V could land on the critical path. The T2 QPRO rung checks this; fallbacks are warps 4-7 only, or PRE=0.
3. Rank-0 skew. Rank 0 has N=5 vs 4 at C=8, but its extra tile is compute-only and ready after one round trip; worst case +0.3-0.5 us. STAGES=5 puts all of its gathers in flight at once.
4. Cluster scheduling at about 112 KB smem. The C=16 non-portable size and 32 clusters of 8 at B=32 are gated by cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters. Fallbacks: C=8 at B=1, C=4 at B=32.
5. The per-tile slope may not be shared bandwidth. If today's 2.1 us per extra tile is per-CTA latency, C=8 vs stream-K is neutral at best and C=16 at B=16 (256 CTAs) wins. If it is bandwidth, the full-line mapping matters more. The T2 chain rung tells which.
6. Registers. The loop must stay at or under 128 registers (launch_bounds(256,2)). Prologue and merge live ranges do not overlap the loop's sacc/oacc, but ptxas may hoist. The attrs line must show local 0; a spill only costs time, and the gate still races.
7. Correctness hazards new to this design:
   - generic -> async proxy ordering for the smem tile;
   - the ring alias after the last wgmma;
   - DSMEM lifetime (the second barrier);
   - no early return or timeout path skipping a cluster barrier (otherwise a cluster deadlock at prepare, which the WAIT_LIMIT abort turns into garbage plus error word 2 and a fallback);
   - the tail-aligned mask at short seq (emulator cases 0..65 and 2040..2056).
8. Schedule claims may not transfer (the X1 lesson). T1/T2 tonight plus the in-run gate are the rungs, and the race guarantees no loss below the incumbent.
9. Import-time growth (about +40-70 s) eats into the margin left by the onepass base (306 s import). Deadlines skip swf before they threaten the 480 s rule.
10. Decode port: the size budget, whether the QKV GEMM triggers PDL early, and co-residency of swf CTAs with GEMM CTAs. All are raced or measured in stage 3.
11. Interaction with the other designer's main-loop rewrite. swf keeps the board's tile body, so a faster body drops in unchanged. If that rewrite lands first, re-time the anatomy before claiming the slope part.

(a) dg_cmerge<C, MERGE>:
- Each CTA loads cache_seqlens[b] cold, fills O[128 rows][64], m and l with a deterministic hash of (b, rank, row, dim) (some m = -inf), then runs the exact swf epilogue: barrier.cluster arrive, gate loads, wait; DSMEM reduce-scatter in rank order; v_scale/L, RMS, sigmoid(gate); bf16 store; second barrier.
- MERGE=0 skips the barriers and DSMEM and writes its own rows.
- Cases (B,C): (1,16), (1,8), (16,8), (16,16), (32,4), (32,8). For each, print cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters and cold-L2 interleaved graph medians (21 reps, empty graph subtracted) of null, MERGE=0 and MERGE=1. Check the output against a torch recomputation of the same hash partials: rel L2 < 1e-3.

(b) dg_chain<C, FULLLINE, QPRO>:
- The swf prologue on _ps_synthetic B x 80000 inputs: seqlen -> page-index block -> tail-aligned gathers of the CTA's tiles into the 5-stage ring (refill at C=4) -> wait all -> per-CTA XOR checksum. With QPRO=1, the cos/sin table, q fragment words into QS and rank 0's new K/V (cache store + stage-0 rows) also run in the gathers' shadow.
- Print per band (B=1 C16, B=16 C8, B=32 C4): half-line vs full-line, full-line + QPRO, and null.
- Correctness, all on the GPU against torch:
  - checksums equal a torch checksum of the same rows (validates the partition and index math);
  - the QS words decode to _ps_prepare_q's e4m3 q with a code gap <= 1 (validates the fragment mapping, RMS and RoPE);
  - the new cache rows match the Triton pre-attention's rows with a code gap <= 1.

Decision rules:
- merge (MERGE=1 - MERGE=0) <= 1.2 us at (16,8) and (32,4) and <= 1.0 at (1,16): build stage 1 as specified. Between 1.2 and 2.5: build, but discount B=16/32 by the excess. Above 2.5: stage 1 becomes swf-pdl.
- QPRO delta <= 0.3 us: fold as specified. Above 0.5: q prologue on warps 4-7 only.
- full/half <= 0.97: FULLLINE=1 (default 1 either way).
- chain(B=1, C=16) >= 8 us: the B=1 claim drops to the low case.
- An occupancy shortfall at C=16 or (32,8) removes those candidates.

Cost and payoff: T2 is about 60% of stage 1's new code (prologue and merge), proven on the judge tonight, which cuts stage 1 to about 2.5 h. T1 and T2 can share one check; each prints at most 3 lines per case, so everything stays in the 14 KB tail.
designs.open_questions:
1. Is today's 2.1 us per extra tile per CTA (7f481040) shared-bandwidth bound or per-CTA latency bound? It decides whether C=16 at B=16 (256 CTAs, 2 tiles each) beats C=8, and how much the full-line mapping is worth. The T2 chain rung answers it.
2. Should stage 1 also race PRE=0 as an attribution and fallback arm? PRE=0 keeps the pre-attention node, PDL-launches swf, reads q8 and gathers the new rows from cache_loc. Default: no, to save build time; add it only if T2's QPRO delta exceeds 0.5 us.
3. B=1 form: one cluster of 16 with both heads per CTA (this design), or PERHEAD 2 x 16 with one kv head per CTA, like decode-1's routed kernel? Stage 2 decides from stage 1's B=1 readout.
4. Decode: does _dsa_gemm('qkv_gate') issue griddepcontrol.launch_dependents early, and can swf CTAs (112 KB) co-reside with its tail CTAs? This sets the stage-3 PDL gain (0 to about 3 us per sliding verify row).
5. Ordering with the other designer's main-loop rewrite. swf is orthogonal: it keeps the tile body and replaces launches, prologue and merge. If both land, re-run the anatomy before stacking claims.
6. FA3 full-verify fixed cost (verify 1 full 34.2 / 36.3, the worst row) is outside this angle. swf's window=0 form does not fit 80K keys per request without a grid-wide merge, so leave it to the other design.

designs.title: Full verify B=1 off FA3: the window kernel at window 0 with every tile requested up front, plus a per-row PDL merge that also does the norm-gate, raced against FA3 (FA3 stays wherever it streams better)
designs.angle:
Designer 2: replace FA3 at small B. The scored small-B full row is full verify B=1 (weight 16). It runs 30.09 us net against a 4.28 us floor, the worst ratio on the board (1.208x vs SGLang). FA3 spends it like this: prepare_varlen 2.8 + main 14.8 + FlashAttnFwdCombine 6.8 + norm_gate 1.0 + pre-attn 1.6 us of kernels across 5 graph nodes (board 4e386647, profile index 7).

How the angle's two FA3 savings are taken legally. The anatomy run f1043d2c measured num_splits=1 at -2.2/-2.6 us and precomputed scheduler metadata at -2.2/-2.4 us (B=16/32), but metadata built from input lengths may not be cached. Here the tile schedule is a closed-form function of cache_seqlens that both kernels recompute every call (window_tile_prefix / start_of / owner_of). So there is no prepare_varlen node and no cached metadata. FA3's split combine and the separate norm-gate become one merge kernel launched under PDL.

A literal single split cannot work at B=1. One CTA per kv head would stream 20.5 MB with 2 CTAs. So the split is stream-K over all SMs, with a cheap merge.

Shared skeleton: the attention kernel is slidewin_verify_wgmma_kernel<MODE_SPLIT> itself, at window = 0. It is the board's routed sliding-verify kernel, and the board's import self-check already validates it at window 0. Only the ring depth is templated.

FA3 stays routed for B >= 2. At B=16/32 FA3 streams at 2.58 TB/s (e8aac4b8) and the window skeleton's stream there has never been measured cleanly. Stage 1 times it print-only, and tonight's diagnostic measures it with zero new CUDA.
designs.summary:
Full verify B=1 moves to a new module, muse_full_verify_sb. The path becomes [existing unpaired _pre_attention_kernel] then fvs_attn_kernel<STG>, then fvs_combine_kernel<16, PDL>.

- **fvs_attn_kernel<STG>** is a copy of the board's window kernel (SPLIT path, window 0). The only changes: the ring depth STG is a template parameter (5 vs 4) and IDX_TILES is 8. At grid 2xSM each CTA owns 4-5 64-key tiles of the 80,008 keys. With STG=5, all of them are requested before the first wait.
- **fvs_combine_kernel** is c320's proven ONEPASS combine, re-indexed for verify partials and the window kernel's stream-K slots. It runs one CTA per (token, q head) row, 16 warps each, merges 132-264 slots, and does RMSNorm x sigmoid(gate). It is launched with PDL from the same C++ call.

Effect on the graph: 5 nodes become 3. prepare_varlen, the FA3 main kernel, FlashAttnFwdCombine and norm_gate are gone. There are no tickets, no atomics, and no in-kernel merge, so this is not the refuted 'tk'.

Routing:
- The route is config-only (B == 1, window 0, q_len 8, page 1, tp8). It is frozen at import after an in-run race against kernel_fn's real FA3 path on the judge's exact B=1 shape: two 31-rep rounds, >=1.05x in both, an IQR bound, agreement < 3e-2, and a two-state replay.
- No test hits the route, so the 16 tests are unaffected.
- B=16/32 are timed print-only. They route only if tonight's diagnostic shows the window pair >=1.05x faster than paired FA3.

- Stage 2 (fused prologue, shape-only partition): ~14.5 us, +4.3% cumulative.

- Stage 4: decode port of the same chain, about +0.36% on decode.

designs.mechanism:
ROUTE (stage 1)
Applies to full verify with window 0, rope 0, q_len 8, page_size 1, hq 16, hkv 2, d 64, batch == 1. The launches:
1. Today's unpaired _pre_attention_kernel[(8, 18)] with ROPE False and PAIRED False, exactly as kernel_fn line 1882 issues it. It writes q e4m3 [8, 16, 64] and the 8 new K/V rows.
2. One C++ call that launches fvs_attn_kernel<STG> (grid G, 256 threads, dynamic smem SMEM_A(STG)), then fvs_combine_kernel<16, true> (grid (8, 16), 512 threads) with cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization.

That is 3 graph nodes instead of 5.

ATTENTION KERNEL = the window kernel, verbatim math
Source: copy _SW_CUDA lines 7860-8131 (constants and helpers, minus merge_head) and slidewin_verify_wgmma_kernel lines 8140-8523, with these edits only:
- template <int STG> replaces STAGES everywhere;
- IDX_TILES = 8 (IDX_N 512);
- smem offsets become constexpr functions of STG;
- the MODE parameter, the ticket parameter and the MODE != SPLIT block (8496-8515) are removed;
- griddepcontrol.launch_dependents stays right after window_tile_prefix.

Decomposition:
- Keys [0, cache_seqlens) form T = ceil(seq/64) 64-key tiles.
- One 128-byte cache row holds both kv heads. A CTA loads whole rows, and warpgroup g owns kv head g.
- M = 64 rows = 8 tokens x 8 q heads, one m64 wgmma tile.
- S = Q K^T and O += P V are each 2 wgmma.m64n64k32.e4m3 calls. Q A-fragments are staged in smem once per segment and reloaded every tile.
- V^T is built per warpgroup in a SW64 buffer.
- P = exp2(s - (max - 8)) in e4m3 (FA3's Max_offset), with an fp32 online softmax.
- Stream-K: CTA c owns tiles [floor(cT/G), floor((c+1)T/G)). At B=1 with T = 1251: G = 264 gives 4-5 tiles per CTA, G = 132 gives 9-10.
- Causal mask: key t is valid for token j iff t <= seq - 8 + j. It only touches the last tile(s).

Data movement:
- Each tile is 16 KB, copied with 16-B cp.async.cg into an STG-stage SW128 ring.
- Page indices load in 8-tile blocks (4-B cp.async, double buffered).
- STG=5 needs smem 111,472 + 1,024 = 112,496 B, so 2 x (112,496 + 1,024) = 227,040 <= 233,472 and 2 CTAs/SM hold. The prologue issues 4 tiles and iteration 0's refill issues the 5th with no EMPTY wait (n = 0). So a B=1 CTA has every tile in flight before its first FULL wait: 160 KB per SM.
- STG=4 (96,096 B) has its 5th tile waiting for tile 0's release, which costs one extra exposed DRAM latency for about 74% of CTAs. STG=4 is kept as the in-run control.

Partials:
- Slot bx + cb holds o fp32 [8, 16, 64] plus (m, l) [2, 128].
- That is 33 KB per CTA: 8.6 MB at G=264, 4.3 MB at G=132. It stays L2-resident.
- Workspaces are torch.empty per call: (G + B, 8, 16, 64) and (G + B, 2, 128) fp32, out (B, 8, 1024) bf16, all shape-only.

Synchronization:
- Per-stage FULL (256 noinc arrivals) and EMPTY (256 arrivals) mbarriers with bounded waits.
- An error word (int32, device-global, written only on a timeout or bad shape, read only at import).
- A named barrier per warpgroup for V^T.
- No atomics, no tickets, no grid-wide sync.

COMBINE = c320_combine_kernel ONEPASS (submission.py:6496-6636) re-indexed
template <int NW, bool PDL>, grid (B*8, 16), block NW*32. Shared memory: seq_s[64], lo_s[64], pre_s[68], vld[1024] (u8), red_m[NW], red_l[NW], red_acc[NW][64].

Steps:
1. window_tile_prefix(seqlens, B, 0, ...), as sw_combine at 8549. b = x/8, j = x%8, h = y. T = pre[B], x0 = pre[b], x1 = pre[b+1]. c_lo = owner_of(x0), c_hi = owner_of(x1 - 1), n = c_hi - c_lo + 1.
2. Thread i sets vld[i] = start_of(c_lo + i) < start_of(c_lo + i + 1), then a CTA barrier. Ranges are contiguous and ordered: c_lo's range holds x0 and c_hi's holds x1 - 1. So every non-empty CTA in [c_lo, c_hi] covers request b. The host checks G <= 1024.
3. Inputs-only loads: v_scale and this lane's 2 gate logits.
4. griddepcontrol.wait (PDL only).
5. Warp w folds slots i = w + NW*t in groups of 16. For every valid one it issues __ldcg loads of m = ws_ml[(c+b)*256 + j*16 + h], l = [... + 128] and the float2 ws_acc[(((c+b)*8 + j)*16 + h)*64 + 2*lane] before any use, then runs an online LSE: an m = -inf slot weighs 0, and alpha = ex2(Mw - Mn).
6. Warp 0 merges the NW warp states in index order.
7. o / L x v_scale, then scaleless RMSNorm over 64 (eps inside the sqrt, a 32-lane xor sum), x sigmoid(gate), stored as bf16x2.

All partials share the window kernel's log2 units and 2^8 offset, so the offset cancels in o/L. The fold order is fixed, so the output is bitwise reproducible. PDL and plain launches are identical code apart from the wait.

GATING
- kernel_fn gets one line after line 1844: if _FVS_ROUTE and _fvs_gate(cfg): return _fvs_forward(data). The predicate is config-only and _FVS_ROUTE is an import-frozen MappingProxyType {"B=1": (stg, grid spec, nw)}.
- The route is chosen by an in-run race against kernel_fn(data) with the route off, which is the real FA3 path, on the judge's exact B=1 shape: seq_lens 80000, page 1, scattered pages.

WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE REFUTED 'tk' (FINDINGS do-not-try)
'tk' merged inside the attention kernel. The last-arriving 128-thread warpgroup of each (request, kv head), after a fence and an atomic ticket, read every slot of its request serially on the attention kernel's tail. In s2b that measured merge +21.6 us vs +3.0 for the PDL split; s6's ticket epilogue cost ~107 us at B=16. At B=1 it would be 264 slots x 16 KB through 128 threads per head.

This design has no in-kernel merge. The merge is a separate kernel that starts after the attention grid completes. It is spread over 128 CTAs x 512 threads, one CTA per output row, with every load issued before use. It is the 'pdl' family the board already routes, re-gridded for 132-264 slots per request. Reusing sw_combine_kernel's (B*8, 2) grid would give 16 CTAs folding 264 slots each in 33 serial batches.

The stale running item full-verify1-wgmma-s7-grid-sm-two-level (s6 kernel plus a two-level ticket) is the 'tk' family and is superseded by this design.

designs.rules:
1. **CUDA graph:** the new kernel_fn branch is a config-only predicate over an import-frozen MappingProxyType. Its launches use grids from the SM count and workspaces sized torch.empty((G+B, ...)) from shapes only. The PDL launch sits inside one C++ call; graph capture of that pattern is already proven by the routed sw pair. There is no host sync, print, try, Python state or data-dependent Python control flow in kernel_fn.
2. **Nothing cached from data:**
   - No tickets, counters or flags.
   - Every partial slot the combine reads is written in the same call. Its validity is recomputed from this call's cache_seqlens.
   - The tile schedule (the legal stand-in for FA3's scheduler metadata) is recomputed inside both kernels every call. Nothing derived from lengths survives a call.
   - The error word is fault-only and never read by kernel_fn.
3. **Precision:**
   - KV stays e4m3 as given; queries are e4m3, as FA3; P is e4m3 with Max_offset 8, exactly FA3's FP8 path in SGLang's own kernel (and already on the board's routed sliding route).
   - Accumulators, partials and the merge are fp32; output is bf16.
   - The cross-CTA reduction is order-deterministic: per-slot partials and a fixed fold order. PDL and plain launches are bit-identical, and rerun is bit-identical; both are checked.
4. **Every key:** [0, cache_seqlens) per token, with causal masking only inside the 8-token block. A slot weighs 0 only when every key in it is causally masked for that row, never by attention weight. No top-k, sparsity or block skipping.
5. **Output within tolerance:** self-check < 2e-2 vs fp32 including a coherent-style 80k case; FA3-level error on the judge (bound 0.15).
6. **All work in kernel_fn:** the race and checks are import-time on our own synthetic tensors (no reference import). The phase is ~90-100 s, so import ends ~400 s on X against the 480 s rule. Total run ~700 s vs the 900 s limit, with deadline skips.
7. **Prohibited actions:** no timing patches, harness access, subprocesses or network.
8. **Size:** ~583 KB, under 1 MB.
9. **Two-state rotation:** no device pointer, tensor map or state-sized buffer in globals; the replay check exercises it.
10. **Raced against the incumbent:** kernel_fn's actual path, on the judge's exact B=1 shape. This applies the num_splits lesson: the 849f2733 race measured 1.46x on non-judge length distributions and the judge's rows did not move. PATH lines name the routed arm.

designs.risks:
1. **Per-tile chain slower than hoped.** The window kernel measures ~2.1 us per extra tile per CTA on sliding B=8..32 at 1 CTA/SM, partly from request-boundary Q reloads that B=1 does not have. If it holds at B=1, stage 1 lands ~21 us (+2.3%), not 17. Tonight's tile-count curve and the L2-warm measurement size this before the build. Stage 3 targets it.
2. **Fault in new code.** The combine's indexing is the main source. A fault poisons the context and fails the check. Mitigations: CPU emulation of every index, host TORCH_CHECKs on workspace sizes, -lineinfo, the canary first, a print around every self-check launch, and a check (never a submit) as the first run.
3. **Prepare-time race misleads.** In 849f2733 the num_splits=16 route measured 1.46x in prepare and the judge's row did not move. Here the race uses the judge's exact B=1 shape (seq 80000, page 1, scattered) and kernel_fn itself as the incumbent. The attempt must read the judge's profile row for fvs kernels, not just the PATH line.
4. **Accuracy on the coherent 80k tail with FP8 P.** The scored full rows are 'dist coherent'. Mitigations: Max_offset 8 (as FA3), a coherent-style self-check case, and FA3 agreement < 3e-2. The judge checks every timed call, so a miss fails the run rather than falling back.
5. **Shared memory at STG 5.** It needs 112,496 B per CTA, leaving ~6 KB of margin for 2 CTAs/SM. If attrs print CTAs/SM = 1, STG 5 is refused and STG 4 races alone.
6. **Grid 264 fixed penalty.** 9.5 vs 7.6 us at K=8 (7f481040), and partials are 8.6 MB at 264 slots. Grid 132 is in the race, and the cluster pair is stage 3.
7. **Import clock.** About +90-100 s (one compile ~45-60 s). Deadlines skip phases and leave FA3. Run total ~700 s vs 900 s.
8. **Overlap with the other designer.** The window-path rewrite edits the same skeleton. A separate module and a single kernel_fn line avoid conflicts; the two are unified later.
9. **B=16/32 stay on FA3** unless measured faster. Upside left on the table, not a regression.
10. **Decode port blocked by size.** Stage 4 waits for the trim.

- Indices: b = blockIdx.x / C, rank = blockIdx.x % C. Warpgroup g = kv head; w = warp & 3, r = lane >> 2 (token), tig = lane & 3, hA = 8g + 2w.

SMEM (base rounded up to 1024)
- RING: 5 stages x 16 KB (K then V, rows of 128 B, SW128: chunk c of row tt at (c ^ (tt & 7)) << 4).
- VT [2 heads][2 bufs][4 KB].
- QS u32 [8 words][256 threads] (8 KB): the board's per-thread A-fragment layout.
- CS float2 [8 tokens][32 pairs] (2 KB).
- IDX int32 [8 tiles x 64] (2 KB).
- FULL[5] and EMPTY[5] mbarriers (count 256), plus flags.
- About 110.7 KB, plus 1 KB slack = 111.7 KB, so 2 CTAs/SM fit.
- After the loop, the partials alias the drained ring: O fp32 [128 rows = token*16 + head][stride 68] plus M[128], L[128] = 35,840 B.

DECOMPOSITION (window W=2048, QL=8)
- seq = cache_seqlens[b] - 8. The old keys are [max(0, seq-2047), seq).
- NT = ceil(min(seq, 2047) / 64) old tiles, counted from the end: tile t = positions [seq-64(t+1), seq-64t).
- Rank r owns old tiles [floor(r*NT/C), floor((r+1)*NT/C)): exactly 2 / 4 / 8 at NT=32, C=16/8/4.
- Rank 0 also owns virtual tile v=0, the 8 new keys (positions seq..seq+7) in ring stage 0. Its old tiles are v=1..n; other ranks use v=0..n-1.
- Ring logic is the board's with STAGES=5: tiles v=0..4 are in flight before the first wait; the refill at n>=1 waits EMPTY parity ((n-1)/5)&1.
- Ranks with no tiles skip the loop with m = -inf, l = 0, but still run both cluster barriers.

MASKS
- Old tile t, column ct, token r: valid iff ct >= 64(t+1) - seq AND ct >= 64(t+1) + r - 2047. The test runs only when 64(t+1) > min(seq, 2040).
- New tile: valid iff ct <= r (ct < 8).
- Gathers zero-fill rows whose position is < 0 (src-size 0). Page indices are clamped into the cache.

PROLOGUE (the order is the point)
1. Entry:
   - thread 0 initialises the mbarriers, then fence.mbarrier_init;
   - all threads issue the independent loads: cache_seqlens[b];
   - PRE=1: own q words (8 x 8 B bf16 from qkv token 8b+r, heads hA and hA+1, dims 32kk + 16jj + 4tig..+3) and positions[8b + (tid>>5)];
   - rank 0 also loads its new k/v pairs (warp = token, lane = RoPE pair: 4 bf16x2) and cache_loc;
   - PRE=0: q8 words (the board's qra/qrb addressing).
2. When seq arrives: plain loads of this CTA's page indices into IDX, then __syncthreads.
3. Issue cp.async for every tile that fits the ring (full-line mapping: c = tid & 7, tt = (tid >> 3) + 32j) with noinc arrivals.
   - PRE=0 rank 0: v=0 gathers its 8 new rows from cache_loc (rows 8..63 src-size 0).
4. Only then the fold (PRE=1):
   - CS table: rope_sincos(__fmul_rn((float)positions[8b+j], inv_freq[i])), one entry per thread, then __syncthreads;
   - q: RMS over 64 via quad xor-shuffles (1, 2) (eps inside the sqrt, scaleless), RoPE on the held pairs, e4m3 satfinite without the 5.473 factor, 8 sts32 into QS;
   - rank 0: k = e4m3(RoPE(RMS(k)) / k_scale) and v = e4m3(v / v_scale), stored to k_cache / v_cache at cache_loc[8b+j] and into stage-0 rows 0..7 (SW128); rows 8..63 of K and V zeroed; fence.proxy.async; a plain mbarrier arrive on FULL[0] by all 256 threads.
   - PRE=0: sts32 the q8 words.
5. fence.proxy.async, __syncthreads.

MAIN LOOP
The board's per-tile body, copied (base X L8442-8619):
- refill;
- lds32 qa;
- wait FULL, fence.proxy.async;
- 2 S wgmma (desc kst + 64g);
- V^T byte transpose into buffer v&1;
- wg_wait0, EMPTY arrive;
- mask + online softmax with Max_offset 8 in exp2 units;
- pack P to e4m3;
- fence.proxy.async + named_bar(1+g);
- 2 PV wgmma, wg_wait0.
Only the tile -> position map and the mask change. No segment, request, ticket or Q-reload logic.

EPILOGUE
1. cp.async.wait_all, wgmma wait, __syncthreads.
2. Write O, the quad-reduced l and m per row into the ring alias.
3. barrier.cluster.arrive.release; issue gate loads for the rows this rank finalises; barrier.cluster.wait.acquire.
4. Reduce-scatter: rank r finalises rows [r*128/C, (r+1)*128/C), 16 threads per row (one float4 each). Read (m, l, O float4) from ranks 0..C-1 in order (mapa + ld.shared::cluster, or cg map_shared_rank). Running max M, rescale by ex2(M_old - M_new); m = -inf weighs 0. This is sw_combine_kernel's arithmetic.
5. o * v_scale / L (L > 0, because key p sits in rank 0's new tile); scaleless RMSNorm over 64 (xor 8, 4, 2, 1); times sigmoid(gate) with expf; bf16 store to out[(8b+j)*1024 + h*64 + d].
6. Second cluster barrier: arrive after the last DSMEM read, wait before exit.
There is no early return anywhere. The bounded mbarrier wait sets an abort flag and err bit 2, then falls through to both cluster barriers.

GATING
- kernel_fn: `if _SWF_ROUTE and _swf_gate(cfg): return _swf_forward(data)`, right after the sliding-decode block.
- _swf_gate requires: window 2048, q_len 8, page 1, 16/2 heads, d 64, RoPE on, 1 <= B <= 32, and the band in _SWF_ROUTE (a MappingProxyType frozen at import: band -> (PRE, C)).
- _swf_forward: PRE=0 first calls _sw_prepare_q(data), exactly kernel_fn's pre-attention (SV32 tiled at B=17..32 when routed); out = torch.empty((B, 8, 1024), bf16); one swf_attn call.
- _swf_setup runs after _op_setup and before the [paths] re-print:
  1. build;
  2. attrs;
  3. canary;
  4. self-check matrix;
  5. per-band gate against kernel_fn with the swf route off: a quick 7-rep pass over (PRE, C) candidates plus the lens-0 fixed term and a null node, then two interleaved 31-rep cold-L2 rounds for the best two. Route iff both rounds are >= 1.05x (1.03x at B=17..32), the IQR is <= 1.5x the incumbent's, rel L2 vs the incumbent < 3e-2, and the err word is 0;
  6. _alt_check two-state replay with gate=_swf_gate (under _SAY_MUTE);
  7. freeze _SWF_ROUTE.
- Deadlines on the import clock: build start <= 380 s, checks <= 420, final rounds <= 455, replay <= 475.

PDL
None in attention: PRE=1 is one node; PRE=0 is a plain second node after the pre-attention. Decode (stage 3) PDL-launches the same source after the qkv GEMM, with griddepcontrol.wait after step 3 and launch_dependents after the main loop.

WHY THIS IS NOT tk
- The partials never leave smem: no global write, fence, atomic, counter or reset.
- All C ranks merge, after one hardware cluster barrier.
- C <= 16 and is fixed, independent of the grid.
- tk's merge_head cost +15.8 to +44 us because one 128-thread warpgroup re-read up to 17-264 global slots after an atomic election.

1. The fold may not hide. sv1 lost 1.1 us today because its fold sat on the critical path. swf issues every gather before any fold work, T2's QPRO rung measures the exposed cost, and the PRE=0 arm is raced in the same check, so a fold loss costs only the fold's share (x1.039 -> x1.024).

3. Cluster hang: barrier.cluster has no timeout, so an early return or a skipped barrier hangs the run until the 15-minute timeout. Audit rule: no early return, and the timeout path falls through.

  - b = blockIdx.x / C, rank = blockIdx.x % C;
  - warpgroup g = tid >> 7 = kv head; w = warp & 3; r = lane >> 2 = token; tig = lane & 3; hA = 8g + 2w.
- Smem (round the base up to 1024 B):
  - RING 5 x 16 KB (K 8 KB, then V 8 KB; 64 rows x 128 B; chunk c of row tt at tt*128 + ((c ^ (tt & 7)) << 4));
  - VT [2 heads][2 bufs][4 KB] (the board's SW64 V^T);
  - QS u32 [8 words][256 threads] (the board's word-major layout);
  - CS float2 [8 tokens][32 pairs];
  - IDX int32 [8 tiles][64];
  - FULL[5], EMPTY[5] (mbarrier count 256), abort flag;
  - total <= 111,712 B including slack, so 2 CTAs/SM. static_assert it.
- After the loop, alias the drained ring: O fp32 [128 rows = token*16 + head][stride 68] + M[128] + L[128] = 35,840 B.
- Tile decomposition (W = 2048, QL = 8):
  - seq = cache_seqlens[b] - 8.
  - NT = ceil(min(seq, 2047) / 64) old tiles, counted from the end: tile t = positions [seq - 64(t+1), seq - 64t).
  - Rank r owns old tiles [floor(r*NT/C), floor((r+1)*NT/C)). TORCH_CHECK C >= 4, so each CTA has <= 8.
  - Rank 0 also owns virtual tile v=0 = the 8 new keys (positions seq..seq+7) in ring stage 0. Its old tiles are v=1..; other ranks number their old tiles v=0...

- Masks:
  - old tile t, column ct, token r: valid iff ct >= 64(t+1) - seq AND ct >= 64(t+1) + r - 2047; test only when 64(t+1) > min(seq, 2040);
  - new tile: valid iff ct <= r.
  - Gathers use src-size 0 for positions < 0 and clamp indices into the cache, as the board does.
- Prologue, in this order:
  1. Thread 0: mbarrier init + fence.mbarrier_init.

Store them to k_cache / v_cache at cache_loc[8b+j]*128 + g*64 + 2l (the judge checks these rows) and into stage-0 row j (byte g*64 + 2l through the SW128 map; V half +8 KB). findings.claim: Rank 0's new-key tile adds one tile-chain to the critical path in every band, and the gain model leaves it out. The spec's targets therefore assume a cost that nothing tonight measures. At the judge shapes each request needs 2055 keys, which is 33 tiles of 64. With one cluster per request, the longest chain is ceil(33/C): 3 at C=16 (B=1), 5 at C=8 (B=16) and 9 at C=4 (B=32). The incumbent SPLIT kernel at grid 132 is balanced at exactly 4 and 8 tiles per CTA (528/132 and 1056/132).
findings.evidence:
How the model is built:
- B=16 and B=32 use 'kernel 14.0 / 22.4', which is the incumbent's 4 and 8 tiles per CTA (7f481040 [diag] sw-fixed-anatomy line).
- B=1 uses 'K=8 at grid 16 7.6 + one more tile about 2'. That is 2 tiles, but rank 0 has 3.

spec.rules:
- CUDA graphs: _swf_forward branches only on config and the import-frozen _SWF_ROUTE. It is captured exactly as the routed sliding_cluster_kernel is. PRE=0 adds the existing Triton pre-attention launch. No .item(), sync, print, try or data-dependent Python. dbg is nullptr on every timed or captured launch.

The only persistent buffer is the error word, written only on fault or timeout and read only at import.

  - FP8 KV as given;
  - q rounded once to e4m3 (as FA3);

The red team's verdict was 'revise': 3 major findings and 6 minor ones. I checked every finding against the code and the runs, and all of them hold. Here is how each is handled.

MAJOR 1: rank 0's new-key tile lengthens the critical path
The red team's claim: rank 0 holds ceil(33/C) = 3 / 5 / 9 tiles, and the gain model left that out. Confirmed. 2047 old keys + 8 new keys = 2055 keys, which do not fit in 32 tiles of 64. The incumbent SPLIT kernel holds exactly 4 / 8 tiles per CTA at B=16 / 32.
Fixed in the design, not only in the numbers:
- The 8 new keys are no longer a ring tile. Rank 0 seeds its online softmax with them in the prologue:
  - S uses 2 mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3, with A = the board's qa words and B = an XK scratch;
  - P uses the tiles' Max_offset-8 scale;
  - PV uses 8 mma.sync m16n8k16 f16, with A = this lane's own P columns and B = an XVT scratch widened from e4m3.
  The accumulator layout equals the wgmma per-warp slice, so the main loop continues from it. The board's decode-1 cluster kernel already attends its new key this way, as a separate 16-key mma.sync tile (mma16832 / mma16816 / attend_tile; base X L4629, L4706-4775, L4849-4905, L4937-4940).
- Every rank's chain is now 32/C tiles (2 / 4 / 8), which is today's chain at B=16 / 32. The seed takes about 0.2 us and runs while the old tiles are in flight.
- Side effect: the ring protocol becomes the board's, uniform over ranks. There is no thread-written stage 0, no plain FULL[0] arrivals, and no stage-0 zeroing or generic-to-async fence.
- Numbers re-derived:
  - central 11.0 / 15.2 / 23.2, x1.036, about 1.671 from base X;
  - best case x1.039;
  - the red team's not-hidden case, 12.0 / 17.0 / 25.2 (x1.022, about 1.648), is now the low case;
  - with the old ring-tile design the central would have been x1.032;
  - EV is about +1.5% (was +1.9%).
- Milestones are set at the low case: v1s <= 12.0, v16s <= 17.0, v32s <= 25.5. The scored-run rule stays tied to beating base X's ranges, now per routed row.
- Readable from one check: a dbg pointer, nullptr on every timed launch, records per-CTA %smid and clock64 stamps in the self-check. They are printed as one [swf-lag] line per band: rank-0 lag and barrier-1 wait.
- Tonight's chain rung now runs the seed itself on the judge. It checks the seed's numerics against float64, and compares rank 0's seed-done with the other ranks' first stage landing. This replaces the red team's optional case that ran the tile body on stage 0.

So placement 2 is expected only at B=1, which carries most of the lever's value. Placement 1 is the knob for B=16 / 32.
